title: Normalized target-shift square for reindexed derived Hom
statement:
theorem derived_target_shift_square
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} X.ProEt] [EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} Y.ProEt] (s : Option ℕ)
    (SX : Closed l E X s) (SY : Closed l E Y s)
    (TX : Models l E X s SX) (TY : Models l E Y s SY)
    (c : Comparison l E g s SX SY TX TY)
    (M N : podReindexingDerived l E Y s) (b : ℤ) :
    c.derived.hom.app (op M, N⟦b⟧) ≫
      (podReindexingDerivedHom l E X s).map
        (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (op ((podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).obj M)))
          (((podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).commShiftIso b).hom.app N)) ≫
      ((CategoryTheory.RingedHomUniverses.hom.{u + 1, u, u, u + 2}
        (ProEt.topology X) (podReindexingRing l E X s)
        ((podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).obj M)).commShiftIso b).hom.app
          ((podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).obj N) =
    (podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).map
      (((CategoryTheory.RingedHomUniverses.hom.{u + 1, u, u, u + 2}
        (ProEt.topology Y) (podReindexingRing l E Y s) M).commShiftIso b).hom.app N) ≫
      ((podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g s).commShiftIso b).hom.app
        ((podReindexingDerivedHom l E Y s).obj (op M, N)) ≫
      (c.derived.hom.app (op M, N))⟦b⟧'

source.place: Step 4; the target-variable part of the representative signed-shift argument in lem-pod-reindexing-shift-derived-model.

proof.text: Identify the inverse of podReindexingHomModel with the fixed ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison. Curry its naturality and transport the first argument along an isomorphism Q(P) ≅ M. The existing rightShift_existsUnique normalization supplies an unsigned target reindexing isomorphism and the exact localization equation for this transported natural transformation.

For the two unsigned target reindexing isomorphisms supplied on X and Y, compare the two chain-level routes after every Hom-product projection. The target-variable Hom functor projection equation removes the termwise shift comparison, whose degree components are identities. Evaluate on sections and on a section of the source module. Comparison.chain_projection converts both sides to the Y projection, and RightFormula identifies them. Homological-complex, product and section extensionality give the chain square.

At a K-injective I and its shift, Comparison.derived_model gives commuting squares between the ordinary-to-derived comparisons and the chain comparison. A general categorical pasting calculation combines these with the two normalized shift equations, naturality, the chain square, and the CommShift equation of podReindexingDerivedFactors.hom. Cancel the invertible ordinary comparison at I[b] and the shifted localization-factor transport. This proves the displayed derived target-shift square for Q(P), Q(I), without leaving any representative obligation.

Use the object bijection of the standard localization to write M literally as Q(P). The independent-universe ringed-site Grothendieck theorem and exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isKInjective give a K-injective I and N ≅ Q(I). For fixed M package the two sides of the target-shift equation as natural transformations in N. The preceding representative square gives equality at Q(I). Naturality along N ≅ Q(I) and cancellation of its image prove equality at N.
